title: Add merge_lock and state_lock parameters to execute_wu()
description: Extend execute_wu() to accept two asyncio.Lock arguments. Wrap the merge_branch() call with `async with merge_lock`. Replace every write_state() site with the acquire→reread→mutate→write pattern using state_lock. There are four write sites: (1) set in_progress at the top, (2) commit verdict in the try block, (3) AgentHaltError handler, (4) bare Exception handler. Sites 3 and 4 already re-read state before writing; add the lock around each. Site 1 and 2 require a fresh read_state() inside the lock so the local `state`/`wu_state` refs are not stale. Re-derive failure_count from the freshly read state inside the verdict lock block.
acceptance_criteria: execute_wu() signature is: async def execute_wu(wu, session_manager, target_repo, context_md, *, merge_lock: asyncio.Lock, state_lock: asyncio.Lock) -> str
merge_branch() is called only while merge_lock is held
All four write_state() call sites acquire state_lock, call read_state() to get a fresh snapshot, apply only this WU's changes to that snapshot, then call write_state()
failure_count is read from the fresh state snapshot inside the verdict lock block, not from the stale top-of-function snapshot
Return type is unchanged (str verdict: 'pass', 'fail', or 'reshape')
The existing except Exception guard still swallows all errors and returns 'fail'

implementer_report.summary: Extended execute_wu() with keyword-only merge_lock and state_lock parameters (asyncio.Lock). All four write_state() sites now follow the acquire→read_state()→mutate→write_state() pattern under state_lock. The merge_branch() call is wrapped with async with merge_lock. failure_count in the verdict block is re-derived from the freshly read state snapshot inside the lock, not from the stale top-of-function snapshot. Updated run_batch() to create both locks and forward them to execute_wu(), keeping the codebase fully functional in this intermediate (pre-TaskGroup) state. No files outside solution_domain were touched.
implementer_report.commit_message: feat(WU-002): add merge_lock and state_lock to execute_wu() for concurrent-safe state and merge operations
